nary_nodes.label: Study on type 2 diabetes in young women
evidence: This was revealed when a team of researchers from Imperial College London evaluated data from an English National Diabetes Audit between 2011 and 2024.
The results, published in The Lancet Regional Health Europe journal, showed the sharpest increase was among white, Asian and Black women in their 20s, and white women in their 30s.

nary_nodes.label: 2026 health report on diabetes in Germany
evidence: From 2014 to 2023, there was an increase in type 2 diabetes cases of 5.8% a year among youth aged 11 to 17 years, according to a 2026 health report on diabetes released by the DDG.

nary_nodes.label: Report on underdiagnosis of type 2 diabetes in women
evidence: In 2025, Kautzky-Willer and a colleague wrote a report for the Deutsches Ärzteblatt, a German medical journal, saying that the disease is underdiagnosed in women.

nary_nodes.label: Rising type 2 diabetes in white populations is a public health challenge
evidence: "Much of the discussion around rising type 2 diabetes in younger people has focused on ethnic minority groups," said Shivani Misra, the lead author of the study and a clinical associate professor for diabetes at Imperial College London.

"While these ethnic groups are disproportionately affected with early-onset type 2 diabetes, we now see that incidence is [...] increasing in white populations too, showing that this public health challenge is broadening across the generation."

nary_nodes.label: Lifestyle factors drive type 2 diabetes in youth
evidence: "We live in a world where we don't move enough and where our nutrition contains too much sugar and too many calories," Gallwitz said. "That leads to more obesity among young people, and that in turn greatly increases the risk of type 2 diabetes."

nary_nodes.label: Underdiagnosis in women linked to testing methods
evidence: "Men are usually diagnosed with [type 2 diabetes] at a younger age," they wrote in the the article. "At the point of diagnosis, more women are obese, they have hypertension more often and have gained more weight" than men when they are diagnosed.

"For one, the value often tested in initial diabetes diagnosis is fasting blood sugar," Kautzky-Willer said. "Your fasting blood sugar is your blood sugar level when you haven't eaten for eight hours. It's just a single snapshot in time, however, and misses blood sugar spikes after a meal."
